{{Short description|Season of Japanese second-tier football}} {{Use dmy dates|date=September 2015}} {{Infobox football league season | competition = Meiji Yasuda J2 League | season = 2015 | winners = [[Omiya Ardija]] | promoted = Omiya Ardija{{-}}[[Júbilo Iwata]]{{-}}[[Avispa Fukuoka]] | relegated = [[Oita Trinita]]{{-}}[[Tochigi SC]] | league topscorer = [[Jay Bothroyd]] (20 goals) | matches = 462 | total goals = 1014 | highest attendance = 20,234{{-}}([[Consadole Sapporo|Consadole]] vs Tochigi SC, 23 November) | lowest attendance = 1,227{{-}}([[Zweigen Kanazawa|Zweigen]] vs [[Ehime FC]], 1 April) | average attendance = 6,845 | prevseason = [[2014 J.League Division 2|2014]] | nextseason = [[2016 J2 League|2016]] }} The '''2015 [[Meiji Yasuda Life|Meiji Yasuda]] [[J2 League]]''' (2015 明治安田生命J2リーグ){{cite press release|url=http://www.j-league.or.jp/release/000/00006269.html |title=新年のご挨拶 |publisher= J.League (Official) |date=2015-01-01 |access-date=2015-01-19 |language=ja |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150104080654/http://www.j-league.or.jp/release/000/00006269.html |archive-date=4 January 2015 }} season was the 44th season of the second-tier club football in Japan and the 17th season since the establishment of J2 League. The season began on 8 March 2015 and ended on 23 November 2015. This was first season of J2 League as renamed from J. League Division 2. ==Clubs== [[Shonan Bellmare]] have stayed in the second division for just a year, winning promotion as the champions. [[Matsumoto Yamaga FC|Matsumoto Yamaga]] have spent only 3 seasons in J2 after promoted from [[Japan Football League]] in 2012, becoming the first club based in [[Nagano Prefecture]] which have promoted to the top flight. Sixth-placed [[Montedio Yamagata]] won the promotion playoffs and will return in the first division after playing in the J2 for 3 years. [[Tokushima Vortis]] were relegated from the J1 immediately after their inaugural promotion, while [[Cerezo Osaka]] and [[Omiya Ardija]] have suffered relegation respectively after five and ten years from their last presence in J2. On the other end of the table, [[Zweigen Kanazawa]] have been promoted from [[2014 J3 League]] as the champions of the inaugural season of the J3 League, replacing relegated [[Kataller Toyama]]. {{location map+ |Japan |float=right |width=450 |caption=Locations of the 2015 J2 League teams |places= {{location map~ |Japan |lat=33.585803 |long=130.461066 |label_size=80|label=
